lesson.title: Critical infrastructure
lesson.summary: Identify the listed infrastructure sectors and their safety-component condition.

prerequisites.reason: Infrastructure in Annex III must not be confused with the Annex I product route.
The listed infrastructure use requires a safety-component function.

blocks: **Critical infrastructure** includes assets, equipment, networks or systems necessary to provide an essential service. The AI Act refers to the definition in Directive (EU) 2022/2557, which links essential services to vital societal, economic, health, safety or environmental functions.
Importance to a business alone does not prove the listed AI use. Begin with the actual infrastructure and service.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(62); Annex III 2; Article 49(5)

blocks: Annex III point 2 lists AI intended as safety components in managing or operating critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
This is a sector-and-function test. Not every AI used by a utility is automatically in point 2. A billing helper and a safety-dependent control function have different intended purposes.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(62); Annex III 2; Article 49(5)

blocks: Fictional Northbridge case: a water service uses AI in a safety function whose malfunction can endanger people. The record identifies the supply function and the safety dependency.
Change the facts to a purely clerical invoice sorter with no safety role. The same organisation's identity does not preserve the safety-component fact. Test actual operation and dependencies.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(62); Annex III 2; Article 49(5)

blocks: If point 2 applies, continue the full Article 6 analysis. Registration also has a particular route: Article 49(5) assigns high-risk systems in point 2 to national-level registration.
Do not turn that registration distinction into an exclusion from high-risk classification. The classification, obligations, registration location and application dates answer different questions.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(62); Annex III 2; Article 49(5)

questions.prompt: A utility buys an AI invoice sorter with no safety role. What does the utility's identity alone establish?

options.blocks: Not the listed safety-component use by itself
options.reason: The point requires the specified infrastructure and safety function.

options.blocks: Automatic high-risk status for every tool
A universal exclusion for utility software
options.reason: A safety-dependent function may meet the listed use.

options.reason: A logo does not establish the function.

options.blocks: Only in the vendor's private marketing list
options.reason: A marketing list is not the statutory registration route.

options.blocks: At national level, without removing classification
options.reason: The provision specifies registration location rather than an exemption.
